stem.text: Let \( f(x) = - \frac{4 \left|{x + 3}\right|}{x - 6} \) for \( x \ne 6 \). Find all critical points of f.

answer_key.label: The only critical point of f is x = -3.

worked_solution.text: For x other than -3 and 6, \( f'(x) = \frac{36}{\left(x - 6\right)^{2}} \text{ for } x > -3 \text{ and } f'(x) = - \frac{36}{\left(x - 6\right)^{2}} \text{ for } x < -3 \). The derivative is never 0.
The numerator 36 is never 0, so \( f'(x) = 0 \) has no solution.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical point where the derivative is zero

worked_solution.text: At x = -3 the function is defined, \( f(-3) = 0 \), and the one-sided derivatives there have opposite signs, so the graph of f has a corner there; so the derivative fails to exist at an input in the domain and x = -3 is a critical point. At x = 6 the derivative also fails to exist, but f is not defined there, so x = 6 is not a critical point.
worked_solution.rule_named: critical point where the derivative fails to exist

options.label: f has no critical points.
options.derivation: f' is never 0, so no critical point was reported, with the corner skipped

options.label: The only critical point of f is x = 6.
options.derivation: the excluded input 6 reported as the only place where f' fails to exist, with the corner missed

options.label: The only critical point of f is x = -3.
The critical points of f are x = -3 and x = 6.
options.derivation: the excluded input 6 kept beside the corner
